title: TP hang repro matrix + results (runtime 1.18.x → 1.19.x)
content:
TP hang repro matrix + results (runtime 1.18.x → 1.19.x)
Owner: Sahana Iyer (Perf-canary/CI)
Last sweep: 2025-03-06

Purpose
- Track which environments + traffic patterns reproduce the “TP group stuck” failure modes.
- Validate fixes landing in 1.19.x (cancel/barrier, async error propagation, watchdog/quarantine) reduce or eliminate hangs.
- Provide quick at-a-glance guidance for: (a) where we can reliably repro in lab, (b) what to run in perf-canary, (c) confidence gates for canary rollout.

Legend / columns
- TP: tensor parallel size (GPUs per group).
- Concurrency: requests in flight per TP group unless otherwise noted.
- Seq mix: prompt_len / gen_len distribution. “Mixed” uses a p50/p95 style distribution.
- Streams: number of HTTP streams (streaming responses) vs non-stream.
- Cancel%: percent of requests canceled mid-stream (client disconnect / timeout cancellation).
- FI: fault injection. “rank_delay(r)” delays a specific rank during collectives/step boundaries. “drop_rank” simulates a rank stop.
- Result: PASS (no hangs), HANG (no forward progress), TIMEOUT (request timeouts but group eventually recovers), RESET (watchdog triggered / TP group recycled).
- Signature taxonomy (rough):
  - COMM_STALL: collective latency spikes, no per-rank progress, NCCL async error may/may not surface.
  - BARRIER_DEADLOCK: cancellation interacts with barrier; one or more ranks waiting indefinitely.
  - KERNEL_STALL: GPU kernel long-running/non-preempt; SM utilization pinned; comm mostly quiet.
  - SCHED_STARVATION: scheduler doesn’t dispatch despite capacity; queues grow; no GPU work.

Quick summary (as of 2025-03-06)
- Pre-fix (1.18.6 / 1.18.7): reproducible hangs on A100 (PCIe + SXM) and H100 SXM under mixed seq + streaming + cancels; hardest repro on L40S.
- With cancel/barrier fix (pr-18441) + async error checks (pr-18455): BARRIER_DEADLOCK largely gone in lab; COMM_STALL still possible under rank_delay FI and extreme overload.
- With watchdog/quarantine (pr-18462): COMM_STALL transitions from “infinite hang” to “RESET” (controlled teardown) if thresholds set aggressively; tuning needed to avoid false positives on long-gen mixed workloads.

Sheet 1: Repro runs (most recent on top)
(Format: RunID | Date | Cluster/Notes | GPUs | GPU interconnect | Driver/CUDA | NCCL | Runtime build | TP | Model | Concurrency | Streams | Seq mix | Cancel% | FI | Duration | Result | Signature | Evidence/notes)

R-084 | 2025-03-06 | lab-h100-02 (dedicated repro rack) | 8x H100 80GB | NVLink | 550.54.14 / CUDA 12.4 | 2.20.5 | 1.19.0-rc3 + pr-18462 + pr-18455 + pr-18441 | TP=8 | llama-70b | 96 | 96 | Mixed: prompt p50=800 p95=3.2k; gen p50=256 p95=1.2k | 10% | none | 2h | PASS | — | No watchdog triggers. p99 collective latency stable. Good baseline for canary.
R-083 | 2025-03-05 | lab-h100-02 | 8x H100 80GB | NVLink | 550.54.14 / CUDA 12.4 | 2.20.5 | 1.19.0-rc3 + pr-18462 (watchdog on) | TP=8 | llama-70b | 128 | 128 | Mixed (same as R-084) | 25% | none | 90m | RESET | SCHED_STARVATION (post-reset) | Watchdog triggered 3x when queue depth > 3k and per-rank progress flat for ~35s. After reset, service recovered; some 5xx during recycle. Indicates threshold too sensitive under aggressive cancel.
R-082 | 2025-03-05 | lab-h100-02 | 8x H100 80GB | NVLink | 550.54.14 / CUDA 12.4 | 2.20.5 | 1.19.0-rc2 + pr-18455 + pr-18441 (no watchdog) | TP=8 | llama-70b | 128 | 128 | Mixed | 25% | rank_delay(r=3, 200ms every 20th step) | 60m | TIMEOUT | COMM_STALL | No infinite hang, but saw repeated spikes in all_reduce p99 (10–25s). Some requests timed out at client. Async error checks logged warnings but no abort without watchdog.
R-081 | 2025-03-04 | lab-a100-sxm-01 | 8x A100 80GB | NVLink | 535.129.03 / CUDA 12.2 | 2.18.3 | 1.19.0-rc2 + pr-18455 + pr-18441 | TP=8 | llama-70b | 96 | 96 | Long-gen: prompt=512; gen=2k | 0% | none | 2h | PASS | — | Previously (1.18.7) could trigger stall here by ~45–90m. Not seen in this run.
R-080 | 2025-03-03 | lab-a100-sxm-01 | 8x A100 80GB | NVLink | 535.129.03 / CUDA 12.2 | 2.18.3 | 1.18.7 | TP=8 | llama-70b | 96 | 96 | Long-gen: prompt=512; gen=2k | 0% | none | 2h | HANG | COMM_STALL | Classic hang: per-rank progress counters flat; one rank shows last log “enqueue all_reduce” and never completes. No NCCL async error surfaced. Requires manual pod restart.
R-079 | 2025-03-03 | lab-a100-sxm-01 | 8x A100 80GB | NVLink | 535.129.03 / CUDA 12.2 | 2.18.3 | 1.19.0-rc1 + pr-18441 only | TP=8 | llama-70b | 96 | 96 | Mixed: prompt p50=1k p95=4k; gen p50=128 p95=1k | 20% | none | 75m | TIMEOUT | COMM_STALL | Some client timeouts; group recovered after ~2–3 minutes of elevated collective lat. Suggests barrier deadlock fixed, but comm stall still present without watchdog.
R-078 | 2025-03-02 | lab-a100-pcie-01 | 4x A100 40GB | PCIe | 535.129.03 / CUDA 12.2 | 2.18.3 | 1.18.6 | TP=4 | mistral-7b | 256 | 256 | Short: prompt=256; gen=128 | 30% | none | 2h | PASS | — | Could not repro on small model; seems tied to long-gen + high TP group size.
R-077 | 2025-03-02 | lab-a100-pcie-02 | 8x A100 40GB | PCIe | 535.129.03 / CUDA 12.2 | 2.18.3 | 1.18.6 | TP=8 | llama-70b | 64 | 64 | Mixed | 10% | none | 2h | HANG | BARRIER_DEADLOCK | Hang correlated with client disconnects. Logs show request cancellation while ranks waiting at step barrier. No further scheduler dispatch. (Pre pr-18441 behavior.)
R-076 | 2025-03-01 | lab-a100-pcie-02 | 8x A100 40GB | PCIe | 535.129.03 / CUDA 12.2 | 2.18.3 | 1.19.0-rc1 + pr-18441 | TP=8 | llama-70b | 64 | 64 | Mixed | 10% | none | 2h | PASS | — | Barrier deadlock not reproduced post-fix. Not enough evidence on comm stalls due to lower load.
R-075 | 2025-02-29 | staging-hosted-us-east (pool: hosted-gpu-large) | 8x H100 80GB | NVLink | 550.40.07 / CUDA 12.4 | 2.20.5 | 1.18.7 | TP=8 | llama-70b | ~110 (observed) | streaming | Mixed (prod-like) | unknown | none | 1h slice | HANG | COMM_STALL | Mirrors Sev1 signature. Needed traffic shift + node recycle. Evidence: “collective_latency_seconds” p99 pegged; per-rank progress flat. (SRE notes: incident 2025-02-13 patterns.)
R-074 | 2025-02-28 | staging-hosted-us-east | 8x H100 80GB | NVLink | 550.40.07 / CUDA 12.4 | 2.20.5 | 1.19.0-rc0 + pr-18455 + pr-18441 | TP=8 | llama-70b | ~110 | streaming | Mixed | unknown | none | 1h slice | TIMEOUT | COMM_STALL | Didn’t fully hang; saw elevated timeouts (~0.8% vs 0.2% baseline). Needed to verify watchdog behavior next.
R-073 | 2025-02-27 | lab-l40s-01 | 8x L40S 48GB | PCIe | 550.54.14 / CUDA 12.4 | 2.20.5 | 1.18.7 | TP=8 | llama-13b | 192 | 192 | Mixed | 25% | rank_delay(r=5, 150ms every 10th step) | 2h | TIMEOUT | SCHED_STARVATION | Queue growth + timeouts; no true hang. GPU util uneven. Might be scheduler fairness rather than NCCL stall.
R-072 | 2025-02-26 | lab-h100-01 | 8x H100 80GB | NVLink | 550.54.14 / CUDA 12.4 | 2.20.5 | 1.18.7 | TP=8 | llama-70b | 128 | 128 | Mixed | 25% | rank_delay(r=3, 200ms) | 90m | HANG | COMM_STALL | Most reliable lab repro for COMM_STALL pre-fix: hang typically within 30–90 minutes.
R-071 | 2025-02-25 | lab-h100-01 | 8x H100 80GB | NVLink | 550.54.14 / CUDA 12.4 | 2.20.5 | 1.18.7 | TP=8 | llama-70b | 96 | 96 | Long-gen | 0% | none | 2h | TIMEOUT | COMM_STALL | Not always infinite hang; sometimes “near-hang” (collectives 20–40s) then recover.
R-070 | 2025-02-24 | lab-a100-sxm-01 | 8x A100 80GB | NVLink | 535.129.03 / CUDA 12.2 | 2.18.3 | 1.18.7 | TP=8 | llama-70b | 96 | 96 | Mixed | 20% | none | 60m | HANG | BARRIER_DEADLOCK | Repro’d deadlock with streaming disconnect patterns (client cancel). Correlates with suspected cancellation/barrier bug.

Sheet 2: Environment notes / setup
- lab-h100-01: DGX H100 (8x H100 SXM), Ubuntu 22.04, driver 550.54.14, CUDA 12.4. Baseline NCCL 2.20.5.
- lab-h100-02: same as above, reserved for “post-fix” verification to avoid cross-contamination.
- lab-a100-sxm-01: DGX A100 (8x A100 SXM), driver 535.129.03, CUDA 12.2, NCCL 2.18.3.
- lab-a100-pcie-02: Supermicro 8-GPU (A100 40GB PCIe), driver 535.129.03.
- staging-hosted-us-east: hosted pool slice, traffic replay from prod traces (partial) + synthetic cancels.

Notes on traffic generator
- Workload generator uses:
  - Mixed seq distribution approximating prod: prompt lengths heavy-tailed; generation lengths spiky due to tool-calling + retries.
  - Streaming enabled by default (SSE). Cancels injected via client disconnect at random token offsets.
- In lab, we control cancels deterministically with a seed; in staging, cancels are “natural” + mild injection.

Current conclusions / hypotheses
1) Barrier deadlock is primarily cancellation-path related
- Strong evidence: reproducible on 1.18.7 under cancel%; disappears with pr-18441.
- Signature: scheduler shows ranks waiting at barrier; no NCCL errors; no GPU kernels running; queue stalled.

2) COMM_STALL requires more than just cancellation (but cancellation increases likelihood)
- Most reliable in H100 + high concurrency + mixed/long gen. FI rank_delay makes it easier.
- Async error propagation (pr-18455) surfaces warnings sooner but doesn’t self-heal without an abort/recycle policy.

3) Watchdog/quarantine changes the failure from “infinite hang” to “controlled reset”
- Good: improves customer-visible MTTR.
- Risk: false positives on legitimately slow long-gen batches; needs threshold tuning by deployment mode.

Open questions
- Can we make COMM_STALL fully disappear (PASS) without relying on watchdog resets? Or is “RESET not HANG” acceptable as interim?
- Do we have a reliable FI that maps to the staging/prod COMM_STALL without overfitting? (rank_delay might be too synthetic.)
- Any correlation with specific NCCL versions on H100? We’ve mostly been on 2.20.5 for H100.

Next steps (owner → target)
- Sahana: wire R-084 scenario into perf-canary nightly (GitHub perf-canary/pr-288 follow-up) → 2025-03-10.
- Marcus: add scheduler starvation instrumentation tags to distinguish post-reset warmup vs true starvation → 2025-03-12.
- Grace/Hiro: evaluate adding explicit “collective stuck” logging w/ rank IDs + last successful seqno → 2025-03-12.
- Rafael: propose watchdog thresholds per Hosted/Dedicated based on R-083 false-positive behavior → 2025-03-13.

How to add a new row (process)
- Use next RunID (R-085, R-086, …).
- Include exact runtime build hash/tag and which PRs are included (if testing cherry-picks).
- Attach at least one piece of evidence in notes: metric snapshot (collective latency / per-rank progress) or relevant structured log line.

Notes to self (cleanup)
- This doc started as a scratch sheet; once the stress suite lands (ENG-2405), we should generate these rows automatically from run artifacts instead of manual edits.
